threads.thread_goal: Align on sitemap, navigation, and page priorities for the redesign.

messages.text:
Kicking off sitemap alignment for the redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.
I have a first pass of the page inventory and target sitemap in the Sitemap and Page Inventory Matrix, based on the audit from T1 and the draft work for T2.
Structure proposal at a high level:
- Top nav: Solutions, Products, Pricing, Resources, Company, Contact
- Utility: Login, Support
- Footer: legal, careers, partner links, etc.
For the first release, I tentatively marked homepage, 2 solution pages, product overview, pricing, resources hub, and contact as must-have.
Please review the entries and navigation groupings in A2 and comment on:
1) Anything missing or redundant
2) Whether the primary vs secondary nav split makes sense
3) What you see as first-release vs later phase.
I have not yet gone deep into mobile nav patterns; this is mostly IA and page list for now.

Thanks for sharing the matrix.
I went through A2 and left comments on:
- Splitting Solutions into Industry and Use-case clusters
- Moving Support out of the main nav into a persistent header link
- Consolidating scattered About content into a single Company section.
Questions:
- Do we have a clear owner for the Resources hub content types yet (webinars, ebooks, blog)?
- For mobile, are you thinking single-level drawer or nested accordion for secondary items?
From a brand and campaign perspective, I would like a dedicated slot in the nav or homepage for seasonal campaigns, but that might be a template decision later.
Let us first confirm the page list and hierarchy, then we can map that into layout work for T4.

I added a few notes in A2 as well.
Two things I am not fully sure about:
- We have both Product overview and Platform overview. Could those be merged, or do stakeholders see them as different stories?
- There are three separate Contact variants (sales, support, general). Maybe we can route via a single Contact page with smart form routing instead of three pages.
For first release, I would lean toward:
- Homepage
- One flagship Solution page
- Product or Platform overview (whichever we decide to keep)
- Pricing
- Resources hub (even if light)
- Contact.
But I might be missing something from the marketing side, so we should validate with them before we lock D1 and D2.

I did a quick pass on the audit notes from T1 and cross-checked with A2.
Some UX gaps I see:
- No clear path from Resources items back into lead forms (especially for webinars and ebooks)
- Pricing is only reachable from Product in the current site; in the new sitemap I would surface it directly in the top nav
- Support content is mixed with marketing content in a few places.
For navigation, I like the primary nav list you proposed. Maybe we can:
- Keep Solutions and Products separate, but ensure each Solution page links to relevant Products
- Put Company and Resources in the rightmost slots so the commercial paths stay prominent.
For first release, I would also consider at least one case study page if we can reuse an existing template quickly.

I have a clarifying question on the Resources hub.
Looking at A2, we have blog, webinars, ebooks, and case studies as separate page types. Are we planning:
- One Resources landing with filters for all of them, or
- Separate landings per type, all linked from the nav?
This will affect how we estimate layout work for T4 and later T6.
Also, for the footer, do we want to mirror the full sitemap or keep it lean with only key sections and legal links?

Good call-out.
My current thinking, based on the notes in A2, is:
- One Resources hub landing with filters for blog, webinars, ebooks, case studies
- Detail templates per content type, but not separate nav entries.
That keeps the nav simpler while still letting us design specific layouts later.
For the footer, I would keep it lean: main sections, legal, careers, partners, and maybe a small Resources cluster.
If everyone is ok with that, I will update T2 to reflect:
- Resources as a single top-level item
- Content types as sub-entries only in the matrix, not in the nav.

I support the single Resources hub approach.
On the Product vs Platform question from M3, my suggestion is:
- Use Product overview as the main commercial page
- Treat Platform as a secondary page that goes deeper into architecture and capabilities, linked from Product and from technical content.
In A2, that would mean Product overview stays in the primary nav under Products, while Platform sits one level down.
For first release scope, I would include Product overview but not Platform; we can add Platform in a later phase once we have more technical content ready.
If there are no strong objections, we can reflect this in T2 and move toward closing D1 and D2 later today.

That split works for me.
I will adjust the notes in A2 so that:
- Product overview is clearly marked as primary
- Platform is tagged as phase two and linked from Product.
On Contact, unless marketing pushes back, I would still prefer a single Contact page with routing.
Maybe we can flag that as a question for the marketing manager when we walk them through the sitemap, before we finalize D1 and D2.

Agree on Product vs Platform and on the Resources hub.
I added a comment in A2 suggesting we:
- Put Pricing immediately after Products in the nav
- Keep Solutions first, since that is how campaigns usually frame the story.
For first release, my proposed list is:
- Homepage
- One flagship Solution
- Product overview
- Pricing
- Resources hub
- Contact (single page)
- Company overview (even if minimal, so the site does not feel incomplete).
If we are aligned, we can present this list to stakeholders as the recommended MVP scope.

From a layout workload perspective, that MVP list is manageable within the 21-day window, assuming we keep the first Solution page and Company overview relatively close to the homepage and Product patterns.
I will keep T4 estimates based on:
- Homepage
- One Solution
- Product overview
- Pricing.
Resources hub and Contact can follow similar structures with some adjustments.
Once D1 and D2 are confirmed, I will sync with dev on any CMS constraints around the nav depth we are proposing.

I have updated A2 and T2 to reflect the latest:
- Primary nav: Solutions, Products, Pricing, Resources, Company, Contact
- Utility: Login, Support
- MVP pages: the list from M9, with Platform and deeper Resources detail pages marked as later phases.
I also added a column in A2 for phase (MVP vs later) so we can track scope creep.
Unless anyone sees a blocker, I suggest we treat this as the target sitemap and navigation model for D1, and the MVP list as D2, pending a quick sanity check with marketing and product.

I just walked through the updated A2 with the marketing manager and product manager in a quick call.
Feedback:
- They are comfortable with the primary nav labels and order
- They agree with the MVP page list you outlined
- They like the idea of a single Contact page with routing.
Based on that, I propose we formally:
- Approve the target sitemap structure and navigation model as captured in A2 (D1)
- Confirm the MVP page list for first release as captured in the phase column (D2).
If no one objects in this thread, we can mark D1 and D2 as decided and move on to layout work in T4.

No objections from my side.
Summarizing what we are locking in:
- Primary nav: Solutions, Products, Pricing, Resources, Company, Contact
- Utility: Login, Support
- MVP pages: Homepage, flagship Solution, Product overview, Pricing, Resources hub, Contact, Company overview.
This matches the latest A2 and T2 updates.
I will keep an eye on any new page requests and log them as later-phase candidates so we do not expand the MVP scope without a trade-off discussion.

Aligned here as well.
I will start mapping the MVP pages to content priorities so that when we get to T6 and T7 we already know which flows need richer content vs placeholders.
For now, I will just add a note in A2 for each MVP page indicating the primary conversion goal, so we remember to design around that in the layouts.

Works for me.
With D1 and D2 in place, I will:
- Sync with the web development lead on the nav depth and any CMS constraints
- Adjust the T4 plan so homepage and MVP pages are clearly prioritized.
I will post any technical risks back here if something in the sitemap proves hard to implement with the current stack.

threads.thread_goal: Select the visual direction and core UI components.

messages.text:
Starting the visual direction and components discussion for Redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.
I have uploaded two moodboard options and an initial component set draft into our design space and summarized them in A3, tied to T3 and T5.
Option A: Clean, minimal, more whitespace, softer color accents.
Option B: Bolder color blocking, stronger typography, more expressive imagery.
Core components sketched so far: header, nav, hero, cards, buttons, form fields, testimonial blocks, pricing tables.
Please review A3 and share:
- Which option feels closer to our current brand while still modernizing
- Any concerns about accessibility or CMS feasibility for the proposed components
- Preferences on motion and interaction level (we need to stay realistic for the current WebCMS).

I went through A3 and left comments.
Initial thoughts:
- Option A feels safer in terms of aligning with the existing brand guidelines; the typography and color palette are closer to what we have now.
- Option B is more distinctive but might require stronger buy-in from the brand manager, especially on the color saturation.
On components, I like the card and pricing table directions, but I am not sure if our current WebCMS can handle the more complex hero variants you sketched.
Maybe we should validate the hero and navigation components with the web development lead before we lock D3 and D4.

I added some notes in A3 as well.
From a visual storytelling angle:
- Option B gives us more room to differentiate Solutions vs Products using color and imagery
- Option A might feel a bit too close to generic SaaS templates if we are not careful.
However, I share the concern about accessibility and implementation.
For components in T5, I would suggest we:
- Keep the button styles from Option A (better contrast and simpler states)
- Use the card layouts from Option B for Resources and case studies
- Choose a single hero pattern for MVP pages to keep dev effort under control.

From a layout and UX side, I tested a few quick wireframes using both directions.
Observations:
- Option A works well for dense content like Resources and Company; the calmer palette helps readability.
- Option B shines on the homepage and Solution pages, especially with the stronger hero and highlight sections.
For accessibility, Option B needs some tweaks on color contrast for text over backgrounds; I flagged those in A3.
For T5, I would prioritize:
- Buttons (primary, secondary, ghost)
- Form fields and error states
- Cards (content and feature)
- Navigation (desktop and mobile).
We can add more decorative components later once the core is stable.

I am looking at this from the perspective of how much variation we can realistically support in T4 and T6.
If we go full Option B across all pages, we will need more unique layouts and that will slow us down.
What if we:
- Use Option B as the primary direction for hero and key highlight sections on homepage and Solutions
- Use a toned-down variant closer to Option A for content-heavy pages like Resources and Company.
In A3, that would mean one visual direction with two intensity levels, rather than two separate directions.
For components, I would keep the set lean for D4: nav, hero, cards, buttons, forms, testimonial, pricing table. We can treat things like timeline or comparison tables as later additions.

I like the idea of a single direction with intensity variations.
I just spoke briefly with the brand manager and walked through both options.
Their feedback:
- They are open to the bolder color usage from Option B as long as we keep typography close to current guidelines
- They want to avoid introducing entirely new accent colors without a clear rationale.
So my proposal for D3 is:
- Choose Option B as the primary visual direction
- Calibrate it with Option A typography and a slightly reduced color saturation.
For D4, the initial component set would be the lean list you mentioned: nav, hero, cards, buttons, forms, testimonial, pricing table.
Before we mark D3 and D4, any strong objections to this combined approach?

No strong objections.
The combined approach should help us keep the site feeling cohesive while still more energetic than today.
I would just ask that we document in A3:
- When to use the more intense variant (homepage, Solutions)
- When to use the calmer variant (Resources, Company, Contact).
For the component set in T5, I am fine with the lean list, but we should also define at least one banner or announcement strip pattern for campaigns, even if it is simple.

I am on board with Option B as the base, tuned with Option A typography.
I added a few notes in A3 about imagery style so we do not drift into generic stock photos.
For D4, I would like to make sure the testimonial component supports both text-only quotes and quotes with headshots, since that will affect how we design the Resources and case study pages later.
Otherwise, the component list looks good to me.

Works for me as well.
From a UX and implementation angle, the lean component set will help us move faster on T4 and T6.
I will start wiring the sitemap from A2 into basic layouts using the chosen direction once we mark D3 and D4.
One small request: can we lock the button and form styles early, since they impact almost every page and the prototype work in T7?

Agree on locking buttons and forms early.
Once D3 and D4 are confirmed, I will:
- Check the component specs in A3 against the current WebCMS capabilities
- Flag any patterns that might require custom development so we can either simplify or plan for them.
I will also start a small checklist under T5 to track which components have been tested in at least two page layouts, as per the definition of done.

Thanks all for the input.
I have updated A3 to:
- Set Option B (with adjusted typography and color saturation) as the primary visual direction
- Document usage of intense vs calm variants by page type
- Define the initial component set: nav, hero, cards, buttons, forms, testimonial (two variants), pricing table, and a simple campaign banner.
Given the alignment and the brand manager feedback, I am marking:
- D3: Primary visual direction chosen as the calibrated Option B
- D4: Initial UI component set locked as per A3 and T5.
I will also log these decisions in A7 so we have a clear record for future reviews.

Great, I will start applying the chosen direction to a couple of key screens so we can validate it in context during the next design review.
I will also help populate A7 with any feedback we get from stakeholders on the new look, so we can track if we need minor tweaks without reopening D3 or D4.

threads.thread_goal: Review and iterate on key page layouts and prototypes.

messages.text:
Sharing first round of high-fidelity layouts and prototype links for Redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.
What is ready:
- Homepage, flagship Solution, Product overview, Pricing in high fidelity (T4, T6)
- Interactive prototype covering homepage to lead form on desktop and mobile (T7), linked in A4.
Layouts follow the sitemap from A2 and the visual direction and components from A3.
Please focus feedback on:
- Whether the page structures support the main conversion goals
- Any issues with navigation clarity or content hierarchy
- Anything that would block us from moving these into dev after one more iteration.
I will log feedback and decisions in A7.

I walked through the prototype in A4.
Positives:
- The homepage hero and Solution highlights reflect the chosen visual direction well
- The Pricing page structure is clear and should be easy to scan.
Questions and concerns:
- On mobile, the lead form feels a bit long; can we break it into two steps without hurting conversion?
- The navigation between Solution and Product overview might need a more explicit cross-link so users understand the relationship.
Before we move toward D5 and D6, I would like to ensure the lead form flow and mobile nav are solid, since they are critical for conversion and usability.

I added comments in A7 after reviewing the desktop layouts.
A few detailed notes:
- On the homepage, the campaign banner might be competing with the main hero; maybe we can reduce its visual weight or move it slightly lower.
- On the Solution page, the testimonial block is strong, but we might want to add a small CTA under it to keep users moving toward the form.
- On the Pricing page, can we add a short FAQ section below the tables? That often helps address objections.
None of these feel like blockers for D5, but I would prefer we address them in the next iteration before we freeze designs under D6.

I focused on the mobile flows in A4.
Observations:
- The mobile nav drawer works, but the secondary links under Resources are a bit buried; maybe we can surface the most important ones as quick links on the homepage.
- The lead form on mobile feels heavy, as mentioned; a two-step flow with a progress indicator could reduce drop-off.
- On the Product overview page, the feature cards stack nicely, but the imagery might be too large on smaller devices; we could reduce image height to bring more text above the fold.
I logged these in A7 under T7 so we can track them as part of the next iteration.

I checked the layouts against what I know of the current WebCMS.
Good news:
- The card grids, pricing tables, and testimonial blocks should be straightforward to implement
- The hero pattern you used is compatible with existing modules.
Potential risks:
- The two-column FAQ layout on desktop might need to fall back to a single column in the CMS; we should design with that in mind.
- The sticky CTA on mobile could be tricky; we might need to confirm with the web development lead whether they are comfortable implementing it.
I will sync with them and update A7 with any constraints so we can adjust before we finalize D5 and D6.

Thanks for the detailed feedback.
I will make the following updates for the next iteration:
- Test a two-step lead form on mobile with a simple progress indicator, keeping the same fields
- Add clearer cross-links between Solution and Product overview (for example, a short section on each page explaining the relationship)
- Adjust the campaign banner hierarchy on the homepage and add a CTA under the testimonial on the Solution page
- Add a compact FAQ section under Pricing, designed to degrade gracefully to a single column if needed.
I will update the prototype in A4 and log the changes in A7 under T4, T6, and T7.

Sounds good.
Once you push the updated prototype to A4, I would like to run a quick usability check with a few internal users focusing on:
- Discoverability of Pricing and lead forms from homepage and Solution
- Perceived effort of the mobile lead form
- Clarity of the relationship between Solutions and Products.
We do not need a full study, just a short round to validate the main flows before we commit to D5 and D6.

When you update the layouts, could you also:
- Slightly reduce the imagery size on mobile Product overview
- Add one more example of a case study card on the Solution page so we see how the component behaves with different content lengths.
I will help capture any feedback from the quick usability checks into A7 so we have a clear trail leading into D5 and D6.

I spoke with the web development lead.
Their input:
- Two-column FAQ is fine as long as we design a single-column fallback; they prefer we show both in the specs
- Sticky CTA on mobile is acceptable if we keep it simple and avoid complex animations.
So no blockers from their side for moving these layouts toward approval.
I will note this in A7 and make sure T4 and T6 include the fallback specs.

I have updated the layouts and prototype in A4 with the agreed changes and logged them in A7.
We ran a quick internal usability check with five colleagues.
Key findings:
- All participants found Pricing easily from the homepage and Solution
- The two-step mobile lead form was perceived as less heavy; no one dropped off between steps in this small sample
- The cross-links between Solution and Product overview were understood.
Given this, I feel comfortable proposing that the current homepage, Solution, Product overview, and Pricing layouts are ready for approval for development, pending your final review for D5 and any last UX tweaks for D6.

I reviewed the updated prototype and the usability notes in A7.
The flows feel solid now, and the visual direction is consistent across the key pages.
From my side, I am ready to:
- Approve the homepage, flagship Solution, Product overview, and Pricing layouts for development (D5)
- Agree that no further structural UX changes are needed before we freeze designs, only minor content or copy tweaks if marketing requests them (D6).
I will record D5 and D6 in A7 so dev has a clear signal to proceed once handover is ready.

Aligned.
I will do a quick pass with the marketing manager to fine-tune any headlines or microcopy, but I do not expect that to change the layouts.
From a design standpoint, I consider the four key pages frozen as per D5 and D6.
Next step on my side is to help ensure the specs and assets for these pages are complete for T9.

No objections.
With D5 and D6 confirmed, I will:
- Start preparing the dev-facing notes for these four pages under T9
- Coordinate with the web development lead to schedule a walkthrough once the full handover package is ready.
I will also double-check that the prototype in A4 matches the final specs so there is no confusion during implementation.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize content, imagery, and SEO-related design requirements.

messages.text:
Opening the thread to finalize content, imagery, and SEO-related design requirements for Redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.
I have drafted content and imagery guidelines in A6, based on T10, and cross-checked them with the SEO and performance checklist items from T11.
The draft covers:
- Hero imagery, icons, and illustration style
- Tone and style rules for web copy
- Basic SEO structure expectations (headings, metadata placement, internal links)
- Examples of good vs bad usage.
Please review A6 and comment on anything that might be hard to support in layouts or in the current WebCMS.

I went through A6 and left a few comments.
Highlights I like:
- Clear guidance on avoiding generic stock imagery
- The examples of concise vs overly long headlines.
Questions:
- For hero imagery, are we mandating illustration-first, or can we mix photography and illustration depending on the page type?
- On tone, we say conversational but professional; do we need more concrete do and do not examples for technical content vs marketing content?
From a layout perspective, everything seems compatible with what we have in T4 and T6, but we should confirm with the content team that the heading structure rules are realistic for them.

I added some notes in A6 focusing on imagery.
Suggestions:
- Use photography for human-centric stories (case studies, Company) and illustration for conceptual content (Solutions, Product overview)
- Define a small set of approved illustration styles so we do not end up with a mix of visual languages.
On copy tone, I agree we should be more specific for technical content; maybe we can add a short section with examples of how to explain complex concepts in plain language.
For SEO, I would like to ensure we explicitly mention that each page should have a single H1 and a logical H2/H3 hierarchy, since that will influence how we structure content blocks in the layouts.

From the layout side, I checked A6 against the current designs.
Everything seems compatible, but a few points to flag:
- If we require a specific minimum length for hero headlines, we should make sure the hero component can handle shorter variants without looking empty
- The guidance on internal links per page might need to be flexible for shorter pages like Contact.
For T11, I can run a quick pass on the key templates to ensure we have clear spots for metadata, structured headings, and alt text.
I will log any issues in A6 and T11.

I am looking at this from the implementation and content workflow angle.
A few practical considerations:
- For imagery, we should specify recommended aspect ratios and max file sizes to keep performance under control
- For copy, it might help to define character ranges for key elements (hero headline, subheadline, CTA labels) so content writers know the constraints.
I added these suggestions to A6 and linked them to T11 so we remember to check them when validating designs against SEO and performance.

Thanks for the feedback.
I have updated A6 to:
- Recommend photography for human stories and illustration for conceptual content, as suggested, with a note that we can mix them carefully on some pages
- Add more concrete tone examples for technical vs marketing content
- Clarify the heading structure: one H1 per page, logical H2/H3 hierarchy.
I also added a note that hero headline length is a guideline, not a hard rule, and that shorter headlines are acceptable if the layout still feels balanced.
Next step is to run this draft by marketing and the SEO specialist to confirm it works for their workflows before we move to D7.

Looks good to me.
I would just add one more example of good vs bad alt text for images, since that is often misunderstood.
I can draft a couple of examples and drop them into A6 later today.
Once marketing and SEO confirm they are comfortable with the guidelines, I think we are ready to treat A6 as the reference for D7.

I ran a quick T11 check on the homepage, Solution, Product overview, and Pricing templates.
Findings:
- All have clear spots for H1 and H2s; we just need to ensure content follows the hierarchy
- There is room for meta description and key SEO fields in the CMS for each template
- Image placements support alt text without extra work.
I added a short summary of this review in A6 and T11.
From a design standpoint, I do not see anything in the guidelines that would require layout changes.

I checked with the web development lead about the performance-related parts of A6.
They are fine with the proposed image sizes and file weight recommendations, and they confirmed the CMS supports the metadata fields we reference.
I added their confirmation to A6 and T11.
From my side, I am comfortable moving toward approving A6 for D7 once marketing and SEO give the green light.

I just had a short review session with the marketing manager and the SEO specialist, walking them through A6.
Their feedback:
- They agree with the imagery and tone guidelines
- They are happy with the heading and metadata structure
- They appreciate the concrete examples of good vs bad usage.
Based on that, I propose we:
- Approve the web content and imagery style guide in A6 as our reference for this project and future pages (D7).
Unless there are objections in this thread, I will mark D7 as decided and log it in A7.

No objections.
A6 looks solid and should help keep future content and imagery consistent.
I will point the marketing and content teams to A6 whenever new page requests come in, so we do not drift from what we just approved under D7.

Aligned here as well.
I will help ensure that any new mockups or prototypes we create follow A6, especially around imagery and alt text examples.
If we see recurring questions from stakeholders, we can add them as additional examples in A6 without changing the core decisions behind D7.

threads.thread_goal: Confirm handover readiness and rollout plan for redesigned pages.

messages.text:
Starting the handover and rollout planning thread for Redesign of Corporate Marketing Website.
On the design side, I have gone through the Design Handover Readiness Checklist in A5 and started filling in the status for T9.
Current status for the four key pages (homepage, Solution, Product overview, Pricing):
- Final screens organized and labeled in the design tool
- Specs for spacing, typography, and states mostly documented
- Assets exported, but I still need to double-check a few image variants.
For rollout, I know T12 and A8 will define the phased plan; I would like to align on:
- Which pages go in the first deployment batch
- Any dependencies with content and dev that might affect timing
- How we handle rollback if something goes wrong.

I reviewed A5 and added some notes for T9.
From my side:
- Specs look good, but we should add explicit notes about the FAQ fallback layout and sticky CTA behavior
- Assets are mostly ready; I will run a quick check on naming conventions and formats to match dev expectations.
For rollout (T12), my initial thought is:
- Batch 1: Homepage and Product overview
- Batch 2: Solution and Pricing
- Batch 3: Resources hub, Company, Contact.
This would let us test the new experience with a smaller set first and reduce risk.

Thanks for kicking this off.
I have started a draft of the rollout plan in A8, aligned with T12.
Current proposal:
- Phase 1: Homepage and Product overview, with monitoring of key metrics and a simple rollback option to the current homepage if needed
- Phase 2: Solution and Pricing, once we are confident in Phase 1 stability
- Phase 3: Resources hub, Company, Contact, plus any minor template updates.
Dependencies:
- Content team needs at least one week to finalize copy for Company and Resources
- Dev team wants a single walkthrough session once A5 is fully green for the first batch.
We should confirm that A5 is complete for Phase 1 before we sign off on D8.

I like the phased approach in A8.
A couple of questions:
- For Phase 1, are we comfortable launching the new homepage without the new Resources hub yet, or do we need at least a basic version live to avoid dead ends?
- For rollback, do we have a clear plan for how long we keep the old templates available in the CMS?
On A5, I will help double-check that all final screens are labeled consistently and that we have captured the decisions from A7 in the specs, so dev does not have to guess.

From a content and brand perspective, I am fine with the Phase 1 focus on homepage and Product overview.
We just need to ensure that:
- Any links to Resources or Solution pages from those two are either live or temporarily redirected to existing content
- The new imagery and tone follow A6 so we do not have a mismatch between old and new pages.
I will help review the copy and imagery for Phase 1 pages against A6 before we call A5 complete for them.

I have updated A5 for Phase 1 pages based on the comments.
Status now:
- Final screens: done
- Specs: updated with FAQ fallback and sticky CTA behavior
- Assets: checked and renamed where needed.
I also synced with dev; they are ready to schedule the walkthrough once we confirm there are no outstanding spec gaps.
For rollout, I am comfortable with the Phase 1 and Phase 2 grouping you proposed in A8, as long as we handle temporary redirects for any links pointing to not-yet-redesigned pages.

I did another pass on A5 and I agree Phase 1 pages are ready from a design handover standpoint.
Next steps on my side:
- Schedule and run the dev walkthrough for Phase 1 under T9
- Capture any dev questions or small adjustments in A7 so we can keep track.
For rollout in A8, I suggest we explicitly note that we will monitor key metrics (bounce rate, click-through to lead forms) for at least two weeks after Phase 1 before moving to Phase 2.

Good call on the metrics.
I have updated A8 to include:
- Phase 1: Homepage and Product overview, with monitoring of key metrics for two weeks and a clear rollback path
- Phase 2: Solution and Pricing, contingent on Phase 1 stability
- Phase 3: Resources hub, Company, Contact, once content is ready.
Given that A5 is green for Phase 1 and we have an agreed rollout plan in A8, I propose we:
- Sign off that designs are ready for development for the MVP pages
- Agree on the rollout phases as documented in A8.
This would satisfy D8.
If there are no objections, I will mark D8 and log it in A7.

No objections from me.
The combination of A5 and A8 gives dev and stakeholders a clear picture of what is going live when and how we can roll back if needed.
I will stay available during the Phase 1 rollout window in case we need any quick design tweaks, but that should not affect the D8 sign-off.

Aligned.
I will coordinate with marketing to ensure they are ready with any campaign updates tied to the new homepage and Product overview when Phase 1 goes live.
If we see any unexpected behavior in the metrics, we can log it in A7 and adjust future phases without revisiting D8.

Works for me.
I will proceed with the dev walkthrough for Phase 1 and make sure they are aware of the phased rollout plan in A8.
Any implementation questions or minor adjustments will be tracked in A7 so we keep the handover clean post-D8.
